items.title: Loren Schoenberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019

ctx.x: But that was a combination of a biography and a discography. And he had a book out called BG on the Record Benny Goodman on the Record. And I found it in a local library and I started writing him post cards about like where can I find the alternate take of “House Hop” or something like this. Because in those days it was hard to find, I mean there’s no internet, there’s no nothing in the record stores and all this kind of stuff, and so I was very much enmeshed in collecting and getting to meet the musicians who…

know I said oh my God, you know. He went, “Well would you like to come with me.” “Would I like to come with you?” But then how am I going to — my father is going to have to drive back and leave me for three or four hours and then either go back to Fairlawn or go sit somewhere, and I went with Teddy Wilson and I got autographs. It was Lionel Hampton, Gene Krupa, Benny Goodman, Lionel Hampton, Illinois Jacquet played with them, and I think it was George Duvivier or Slam Stewart. And I got all these autographs. And…
